title: Lower Shell Below the Belly Fairing — Impact Damage Investigation

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Investigation of ground impact damage on the lower shell below the belly fairing, giving the measurement method, the mapping record and the decision route into the pre-qualified doubler family or a repair approval request.

sections.purpose: This task gives the investigation of impact damage found on the lower shell below the belly fairing, and establishes whether the damage falls inside the limits admitted by the pre-qualified doubler family.
sections.job_setup_note: Do the investigation with the fairing panels removed and good lighting; a dent that looks shallow through a fairing aperture is routinely measured deeper once the panel is off. Get the depth gauge, the straight edge, the eddy current set and the mapping sheet. Photograph the damage against a scale before anything is cleaned, because cleaning removes the transfer marking that shows what struck the aircraft.
sections.procedure: 1. Photograph the damage against the scale card before cleaning. 2. Remove the belly fairing panels that cover the damage area. 3. Clean the area with the approved agent and dry it. 4. WARNING: DO NOT WORK BELOW AN UNSUPPORTED FAIRING PANEL. USE THE PANEL SUPPORT STAND. 5. Measure the damage length, width and depth with the straight edge and depth gauge, and record all three on the mapping sheet. 6. Measure the distance to the nearest fastener row and to the nearest frame or stringer. 7. Do an eddy current inspection over the damage and for fifty millimetres around it. 8. CAUTION: DO NOT BLEND OUT A DENT BEFORE THE MEASUREMENTS ARE RECORDED. A BLENDED DENT CANNOT BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE ADMITTED LIMITS. 9. Compare the recorded values against the limits in SRM-M-51-10-11-004. 10. If the damage is inside the admitted limits, select the doubler size from the chart and raise the repair. 11. If it is outside, raise a repair approval request with the mapping sheet and the photographs attached. 12. Refit the fairing panels if the repair is not done immediately.
sections.close_out: Make sure the area is clean and that the temporary protection is applied if the repair is deferred. File the mapping sheet and the photographs with the aircraft structural repair record. Record the finding, the measurements and the disposition route in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Do not work below an unsupported fairing panel.

tooling.description: Depth gauge 0-25 mm with straight edge
